guard: the event plane's WILDCARD form rides the same delegation envelope every other pattern rides: a peer that holds spawn cannot hand its child a read or write grant on a pattern it does not itself hold, and the `events.` prefix buys no exemption from the containment walk
why: AFTER-RESTORE REBUILD, and it is not tidiness. The suite runs against `@cotal-ai/auth`'s dist,
so the command builds before each run. mutation-proof restores SOURCE and not artifacts, which
means the last mutant's compiled ledger survives the proof: a graded run leaves a local dist
with the security check removed, and the next thing to import it does so silently. Each
mutation rebuilds after its own restore.
The event plane carries tool inputs and outputs, which makes it the most valuable read on the
mesh, and the tempting shortcut when wiring it is to treat `events.` as a special prefix. Both
mutations here ARE that shortcut, written the way an author would plausibly write it: exempt
the prefix from the containment walk so a session can be armed without widening its spawner.
The property is that no such exemption exists, and the plane inherits the ordinary rule.
WHY THESE MUTATIONS WERE RE-AIMED. They used to land on the CONCRETE form, where the ledger was
the only authority: the door accepted the over-ask and the ledger refused it afterwards. An
own-channel rule now refuses a concrete foreign event channel AT THE DOOR, ahead of the mint, so
a concrete over-ask never reaches the ledger and neither mutation could be observed through it.
The WILDCARD form is what still reaches the ledger, deliberately: `eventChannelPrincipal` decodes
exactly two principal tokens, so a pattern is not an event channel to that rule and is governed
by the envelope alone. That is where an exemption would now bite, and that is where these land.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY, and it is why this command carries a build. The suite imports
@cotal-ai/auth and the manager by PACKAGE NAME and by dist path, so the bytes it executes are
compiled, not the source the mutation edits. Without the build in the command a mutation would
be restored having graded nothing and would report SURVIVED for the wrong reason. The build is
scoped to the one package whose source is mutated. After a run, rebuild before trusting any
other dist-backed suite: mutation-proof restores source, not artifacts.

mutations.name: D1 exempt the event prefix from the READ containment walk
mutations.expectRed: a WILDCARD the peer does NOT hold is refused by the envelope on the READ side
mutations.cell: a WILDCARD the peer does NOT hold is refused by the envelope on the READ side
mutations.note: Scoped to the READ side on purpose: the ordinary-channel attenuation cells use plain names and stay green, so the kill lands on the event-plane cell and names it.

mutations.name: D2 exempt the event prefix from the WRITE containment walk
mutations.expectRed: and on the WRITE side: a peer cannot hand down a wildcard write over another owner's planes
mutations.cell: and on the WRITE side: a peer cannot hand down a wildcard write over another owner's planes
mutations.note: The write half is not symmetry for its own sake: publishing INTO another agent's plane forges frames a reader attributes to that agent by subject.
